extracted.intended_audience: publicists, PR representatives, founders, and spokespeople pitching The Verge
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and sending email pitches to The Verge reporters about consumer-technology stories, covering what topics are on/off-target, what makes good/bad pitches, format preferences, embargo practices, and special considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: consumer technology and gadgets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers consumer technology and gadgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches about consumer-facing devices and gadgets are on-topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: tech-policy intersections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers intersections of technology and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that explore policy implications of technology are of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: platform power and consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers platform power and consolidation issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting on the market power or consolidation of platforms fits the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: cybersecurity stories with consumer impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers cybersecurity stories that have consumer impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security stories should emphasize effects on consumers rather than purely technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: climate-tech with real product
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers climate-tech only when there is a real product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch climate-tech when there is an actual product or demonstrable consumer-facing implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: cultural impact of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge covers the cultural impact of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about how tech affects culture, behavior, and society are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not covered (mostly): pure enterprise software
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure enterprise software is mostly not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B2B-only enterprise product announcements are generally off-topic for The Verge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not covered (mostly): B2B finance/legal tech
rubrics_metrics.description: B2B finance and legal tech are mostly not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizontal B2B verticalized tools for finance or legal audiences are usually out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not covered (mostly): generic 'we have an app' announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic announcements that merely state 'we have an app' are mostly not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches should avoid bland product-launch language and instead highlight a compelling angle or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not covered (mostly): crypto pump pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Crypto pump pieces are mostly not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative crypto PR that aims to hype without substance is unwelcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not covered (mostly): AI hype without verifiable demos
rubrics_metrics.description: AI hype without verifiable demos is mostly not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about AI need verifiable demos or clear evidence of working functionality to be of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pitch: Story angle clear in 2 sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: A good pitch communicates its story angle clearly in two sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the core story idea concise and immediately obvious; 2-sentence clarity is the stated standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pitch: Demonstrates you've read recent Verge coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Good pitches demonstrate familiarity with recent Verge coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant Verge pieces to show the reporter you understand coverage context and why your story fits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pitch: Verifiable demo or product available
rubrics_metrics.description: Good pitches include a verifiable demo or an available product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Verge expects working demos or products rather than paper promises; demos behind NDAs are flagged as problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pitch: Source available on short notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A good pitch ensures a source is available on short notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters need accessible spokespeople or sources for interviews; indicate availability clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good pitch: Multimedia (photos, video, screenshots) ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Good pitches have multimedia ready: photos, video, screenshots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide media assets upfront (linked) so reporters can quickly evaluate and use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad pitch: Mass-blasted to multiple Verge reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass-blasted pitches sent to multiple Verge reporters are considered bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blasting the same message to many Verge reporters; personalize and target a specific reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad pitch: 'Following up' emails
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitches that rely on repeated 'following up' emails are considered poor practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid persistent follow-up messages that come across as nagging; make the initial pitch concise and targeted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad pitch: Demo behind NDA only
rubrics_metrics.description: Demos that are only available behind NDAs are considered bad pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a product/demo cannot be shown without an NDA, The Verge is unlikely to be able to cover it effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad pitch: Crypto/blockchain claims without working product
rubrics_metrics.description: Crypto or blockchain claims without a working product are considered bad pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid speculative crypto PR; show working functionality before pitching for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad pitch: 'Industry-first' claims without proof
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Industry-first' claims presented without proof are considered bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back up novelty claims with evidence; unsubstantiated 'first' claims will be treated skeptically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference: Email to specific reporter, not tips@
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge prefers email to a specific reporter rather than the general tips@ inbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target your pitch to a named reporter; do not rely on generic tips addresses for editor pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference: 150-250 words ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideal pitch length is 150–250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep pitches concise—aim for the stated word range to respect reporters' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference: Subject line specific and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject lines should be specific and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an informative subject that reflects the pitch content; avoid vague or clickbait subject lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference: Multimedia linked, not attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia should be linked rather than attached to the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to photos, videos, and screenshots instead of bulky attachments to ensure deliverability and ease of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference: Spokesperson info at bottom
rubrics_metrics.description: Include spokesperson information at the bottom of the pitch email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contact details and availability for spokespeople in the pitch footer so reporters can arrange interviews quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo practices: embargo acceptance and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verge accepts embargoes; standard embargo windows are 24–72 hours and exclusives are strongly preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one Verge reporter per embargo; embargo violations will end the relationship. Use embargoes and exclusives thoughtfully and obey the agreed window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration: Consumer impact angle
rubrics_metrics.description: A consumer impact angle helps a pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how people will be affected by the product or story—consumer relevance increases interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration: Privacy and security implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy and security implications are relevant to The Verge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight privacy/security effects where applicable; these angles strengthen coverage potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration: Diverse expert voices appreciated
rubrics_metrics.description: Diverse expert voices are appreciated in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a range of expert perspectives to enrich reporting and improve pitch reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration: Marginalized communities' perspectives valued
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspectives from marginalized communities are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of how technology affects different communities and, where appropriate, include those voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special consideration: Climate angle increasingly relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: A climate angle is increasingly relevant to The Verge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, explain climate implications and connect product stories to environmental impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise checklist summarizing key pitch quality markers: consumer tech focus; story angle clear in two sentences; verifiable demo; multimedia provided; spokesperson available; embargo respected; one Verge reporter per pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compact checklist to self-evaluate a pitch before sending: ensure topical fit, clarity, demonstrable product, ready assets, spokesperson availability, and correct embargo/exclusivity handling.
